answer: Each night the navigator plots the stars and writes the chart in the log, and the caravan master checks the chart against the sky before the next march. A jade chart copied from another caravan fails the log: at the vault of the night the stars must match the sky above that very camp, and a copied chart names stars that are not there. Forging a chart means hiring a navigator for a full season, bribing a master and paying 16,900, while the vertex entry in the log is dated nightly, so a chart whose stars were never plotted leads the caravan astray.
